THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Wilfredo Malabanan while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS assistive-tech, and this is a worker's own reading: Wilfredo Malabanan held the role worker in Baguio Textile Mills when the token was minted. MEASURED ON achievements.html's OWN RELATIONS: v_worker_truth (1 row(s) while active -> 0 once kicked, and 0 once deactivated, all on the SAME unexpired token); v_service_provider_truth (declared public-by-design in tools/tenant_declarations.mjs, shared with prove_tenant_refusal: over service_providers); v_worker_achievements_truth (1 -> 1, and all 1 are the subject's OWN rows - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills - a person keeps their record on the way out, because a departure showing up as an ABSENCE is the opposite failure and just as bad). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. A relation this hive had no rows in is reported n/a and never counted as a pass, and the subject's membership row was captured before the first write and restored afterwards with the restoration VERIFIED by re-read. `--teeth` perturbs these expectations and the run then FAILS, so the exemptions are load-bearing rather than a green light.

WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_lxp_au_identity_after_change.mjs (gate `lxp-au-identity-after-change`) - the postgres half of this row's two-eyed instrument, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Hector Salvador while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS oversight, and this is a supervisor's own reading: Hector Salvador held the role supervisor in Manila Electronics Assembly when the token was minted. MEASURED ON analytics.html's OWN RELATIONS: analytics_snapshots (2 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Hector Salvador of Manila Electronics Assembly). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. A relation with nothing to hide is reported n/a and NEVER counted as a pass - 46 tenant tables fell there - and the write control proves the probe can still be accepted where it should be (accepted on pm_assets), so three refusals cannot mean three malformed requests.

THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Wilfredo Malabanan while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_tenant_refusal.mjs - the postgres-instrument lens for this row, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. IT IS NOT THE POSTGRES MCP ON PURPOSE: that connects as `postgres`, which owns every public table and carries rolbypassrls, so RLS is never consulted and the read answers with the foreign hive's rows. A superuser lens can prove what data EXISTS; it can never prove a read was REFUSED. This asks as Jun Salvador (no hive - a solo owner, a SOLO OWNER, so every hive is foreign to him) through PostgREST with a real minted token, and again with only the publishable key as anon, for the rows of Manila Electronics Assembly. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS solo-owner, AND THIS IS THAT PERSONA'S OWN READING (tenant_refusal_report.junsalvador.json). PLATFORM-WIDE IN THE SAME RUN: 68/68 tenant tables, 40/40 hive-scoped views, 13/13 person-scoped tables (no hive_id - the boundary there is the PERSON, which is the shape of the logbook defect), 7/7 by-id (BOLA, the row asked for by its own uuid with no hive filter at all) and 3/3 write-authz (forge/patch/erase into the foreign hive) all refused. A relation with nothing to hide is reported n/a and NEVER counted as a pass - 43 tenant tables fell there - and the write control proves the probe can still be accepted where it should be (accepted on logbook), so three refusals cannot mean three malformed requests.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_tenant_refusal.mjs - the postgres-instrument lens for this row, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. IT IS NOT THE POSTGRES MCP ON PURPOSE: that connects as `postgres`, which owns every public table and carries rolbypassrls, so RLS is never consulted and the read answers with the foreign hive's rows. A superuser lens can prove what data EXISTS; it can never prove a read was REFUSED. This asks as Wilfredo Malabanan (Baguio, a plain member) through PostgREST with a real minted token, and again with only the publishable key as anon, for the rows of Manila Electronics Assembly. PLATFORM-WIDE IN THE SAME RUN: 68/68 tenant tables, 40/40 hive-scoped views, 12/12 person-scoped tables (no hive_id - the boundary there is the PERSON, which is the shape of the logbook defect), 7/7 by-id (BOLA, the row asked for by its own uuid with no hive filter at all) and 3/3 write-authz (forge/patch/erase into the foreign hive) all refused. A relation with nothing to hide is reported n/a and NEVER counted as a pass - 43 tenant tables fell there - and the write control proves the probe can still be accepted where it should be (accepted on pm_assets), so three refusals cannot mean three malformed requests.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_tenant_refusal.mjs - the postgres-instrument lens for this row, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. IT IS NOT THE POSTGRES MCP ON PURPOSE: that connects as `postgres`, which owns every public table and carries rolbypassrls, so RLS is never consulted and the read answers with the foreign hive's rows. A superuser lens can prove what data EXISTS; it can never prove a read was REFUSED. This asks as Jun Salvador (no hive - a solo owner, a SOLO OWNER, so every hive is foreign to him) through PostgREST with a real minted token, and again with only the publishable key as anon, for the rows of Manila Electronics Assembly. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS solo-owner, AND THIS IS THAT PERSONA'S OWN READING (tenant_refusal_report.junsalvador.json). PLATFORM-WIDE IN THE SAME RUN: 68/68 tenant tables, 40/40 hive-scoped views, 13/13 person-scoped tables (no hive_id - the boundary there is the PERSON, which is the shape of the logbook defect), 7/7 by-id (BOLA, the row asked for by its own uuid with no hive filter at all) and 3/3 write-authz (forge/patch/erase into the foreign hive) all refused. A relation with nothing to hide is reported n/a and NEVER counted as a pass - 43 tenant tables fell there - and the write control proves the probe can still be accepted where it should be (accepted on logbook), so three refusals cannot mean three malformed requests.

WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_lxp_au_identity_after_change.mjs (gate `lxp-au-identity-after-change`) - the postgres half of this row's two-eyed instrument, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Wilfredo Malabanan while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS adversary, and this is a worker's own reading: Wilfredo Malabanan held the role worker in Baguio Textile Mills when the token was minted. MEASURED ON hive.html's OWN RELATIONS: hive_members (6 -> 1: exactly the revoked person's OWN row, which is the stricter contract - 0 would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from an outage); logbook (6900 row(s) while active -> 0 once kicked, and 0 once deactivated, all on the SAME unexpired token); v_worker_truth (1 row(s) while active -> 0 once kicked, and 0 once deactivated, all on the SAME unexpired token); v_logbook_truth (6900 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills); pm_completions (534 -> 202, and all 202 are the subject's OWN rows - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills - a person keeps their record on the way out, because a departure showing up as an ABSENCE is the opposite failure and just as bad); v_pm_scope_items_truth (144 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills); rcm_fmea_modes (77 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. A relation this hive had no rows in is reported n/a and never counted as a pass, and the subject's membership row was captured before the first write and restored afterwards with the restoration VERIFIED by re-read. `--teeth` perturbs these expectations and the run then FAILS, so the exemptions are load-bearing rather than a green light.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_tenant_refusal.mjs - the postgres-instrument lens for this row, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. IT IS NOT THE POSTGRES MCP ON PURPOSE: that connects as `postgres`, which owns every public table and carries rolbypassrls, so RLS is never consulted and the read answers with the foreign hive's rows. A superuser lens can prove what data EXISTS; it can never prove a read was REFUSED. This asks as Wilfredo Malabanan (Baguio, a plain member) through PostgREST with a real minted token, and again with only the publishable key as anon, for the rows of Manila Electronics Assembly. PLATFORM-WIDE IN THE SAME RUN: 68/68 tenant tables, 40/40 hive-scoped views, 12/12 person-scoped tables (no hive_id - the boundary there is the PERSON, which is the shape of the logbook defect), 7/7 by-id (BOLA, the row asked for by its own uuid with no hive filter at all) and 3/3 write-authz (forge/patch/erase into the foreign hive) all refused. A relation with nothing to hide is reported n/a and NEVER counted as a pass - 43 tenant tables fell there - and the write control proves the probe can still be accepted where it should be (accepted on pm_assets), so three refusals cannot mean three malformed requests.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_tenant_refusal.mjs - the postgres-instrument lens for this row, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. IT IS NOT THE POSTGRES MCP ON PURPOSE: that connects as `postgres`, which owns every public table and carries rolbypassrls, so RLS is never consulted and the read answers with the foreign hive's rows. A superuser lens can prove what data EXISTS; it can never prove a read was REFUSED. This asks as Wilfredo Malabanan (Baguio, a plain member) through PostgREST with a real minted token, and again with only the publishable key as anon, for the rows of Manila Electronics Assembly. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS adversary: a plain member of a hive, which is what this reading measures (tenant_refusal_report.json). MEASURED ON inventory.html's OWN RELATIONS: hive_audit_log (2066 foreign row(s) existed, the asker saw 0, anon saw 0, own 1536 visible); inventory_transactions (138 foreign row(s) existed, the asker saw 0, anon saw 0, own 166 visible); v_inventory_transactions_truth (138 foreign row(s) existed, the asker saw 0, anon saw 0, own 166 visible); asset_nodes (31 foreign row(s) existed, the asker saw 0, anon saw 0, own 31 visible). PLATFORM-WIDE IN THE SAME RUN: 68/68 tenant tables, 40/40 hive-scoped views, 12/12 person-scoped tables (no hive_id - the boundary there is the PERSON, which is the shape of the logbook defect), 7/7 by-id (BOLA, the row asked for by its own uuid with no hive filter at all) and 3/3 write-authz (forge/patch/erase into the foreign hive) all refused. A relation with nothing to hide is reported n/a and NEVER counted as a pass - 43 tenant tables fell there - and the write control proves the probe can still be accepted where it should be (accepted on pm_assets), so three refusals cannot mean three malformed requests.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_lxp_au_identity_after_change.mjs (gate `lxp-au-identity-after-change`) - the postgres half of this row's two-eyed instrument, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Wilfredo Malabanan while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS adversary, and this is a worker's own reading: Wilfredo Malabanan held the role worker in Baguio Textile Mills when the token was minted. MEASURED ON logbook.html's OWN RELATIONS: hive_members (6 -> 1: exactly the revoked person's OWN row, which is the stricter contract - 0 would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from an outage); logbook (6900 row(s) while active -> 0 once kicked, and 0 once deactivated, all on the SAME unexpired token); pm_assets (30 row(s) while active -> 0 once kicked, and 0 once deactivated, all on the SAME unexpired token); fault_knowledge (6900 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills); v_logbook_truth (6900 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills); pm_completions (534 -> 202, and all 202 are the subject's OWN rows - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills - a person keeps their record on the way out, because a departure showing up as an ABSENCE is the opposite failure and just as bad); v_inventory_transactions_truth (166 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. A relation this hive had no rows in is reported n/a and never counted as a pass, and the subject's membership row was captured before the first write and restored afterwards with the restoration VERIFIED by re-read. `--teeth` perturbs these expectations and the run then FAILS, so the exemptions are load-bearing rather than a green light.

PLATFORM-WIDE IN THE SAME RUN: 68/68 tenant tables, 40/40 hive-scoped views, 12/12 person-scoped tables (no hive_id - the boundary there is the PERSON, which is the shape of the logbook defect), 7/7 by-id (BOLA, the row asked for by its own uuid with no hive filter at all) and 3/3 write-authz (forge/patch/erase into the foreign hive) all refused. trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_lxp_au_identity_after_change.mjs (gate `lxp-au-identity-after-change`) - the postgres half of this row's two-eyed instrument, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Wilfredo Malabanan while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS adversary, and this is a worker's own reading: Wilfredo Malabanan held the role worker in Baguio Textile Mills when the token was minted. MEASURED ON marketplace.html's OWN RELATIONS: v_inventory_items_truth (27 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills); service_requests (8 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills); v_service_request_truth (8 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills); marketplace_listings (declared public-by-design in tools/tenant_declarations.mjs, shared with prove_tenant_refusal: mkt_listings_read). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. A relation this hive had no rows in is reported n/a and never counted as a pass, and the subject's membership row was captured before the first write and restored afterwards with the restoration VERIFIED by re-read. `--teeth` perturbs these expectations and the run then FAILS, so the exemptions are load-bearing rather than a green light.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_lxp_au_identity_after_change.mjs (gate `lxp-au-identity-after-change`) - the postgres half of this row's two-eyed instrument, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Hector Salvador while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS oversight, and this is a supervisor's own reading: Hector Salvador held the role supervisor in Manila Electronics Assembly when the token was minted. MEASURED ON ph-intelligence.html's OWN RELATIONS: hive_benchmarks (8 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Hector Salvador of Manila Electronics Assembly). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. A relation this hive had no rows in is reported n/a and never counted as a pass, and the subject's membership row was captured before the first write and restored afterwards with the restoration VERIFIED by re-read. `--teeth` perturbs these expectations and the run then FAILS, so the exemptions are load-bearing rather than a green light.

THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Hector Salvador while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_lxp_au_identity_after_change.mjs (gate `lxp-au-identity-after-change`) - the postgres half of this row's two-eyed instrument, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Wilfredo Malabanan while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS assistive-tech, and this is a worker's own reading: Wilfredo Malabanan held the role worker in Baguio Textile Mills when the token was minted. MEASURED ON public-feed.html's OWN RELATIONS: v_community_posts_truth (declared public-by-design in tools/tenant_declarations.mjs, shared with prove_tenant_refusal: over community_posts (public feed)). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. A relation this hive had no rows in is reported n/a and never counted as a pass, and the subject's membership row was captured before the first write and restored afterwards with the restoration VERIFIED by re-read. `--teeth` perturbs these expectations and the run then FAILS, so the exemptions are load-bearing rather than a green light.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_lxp_au_identity_after_change.mjs (gate `lxp-au-identity-after-change`) - the postgres half of this row's two-eyed instrument, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Wilfredo Malabanan while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS adversary, and this is a worker's own reading: Wilfredo Malabanan held the role worker in Baguio Textile Mills when the token was minted. MEASURED ON shift-brain.html's OWN RELATIONS: v_worker_truth (1 row(s) while active -> 0 once kicked, and 0 once deactivated, all on the SAME unexpired token); shift_plans (2 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. A relation this hive had no rows in is reported n/a and never counted as a pass, and the subject's membership row was captured before the first write and restored afterwards with the restoration VERIFIED by re-read. `--teeth` perturbs these expectations and the run then FAILS, so the exemptions are load-bearing rather than a green light.

A superuser lens can prove what data EXISTS; it can never prove a read was REFUSED. This asks as Wilfredo Malabanan (Baguio, a plain member) through PostgREST with a real minted token, and again with only the publishable key as anon, for the rows of Manila Electronics Assembly. PLATFORM-WIDE IN THE SAME RUN: 68/68 tenant tables, 40/40 hive-scoped views, 12/12 person-scoped tables (no hive_id - the boundary there is the PERSON, which is the shape of the logbook defect), 7/7 by-id (BOLA, the row asked for by its own uuid with no hive filter at all) and 3/3 write-authz (forge/patch/erase into the foreign hive) all refused. A relation with nothing to hide is reported n/a and NEVER counted as a pass - 43 tenant tables fell there - and the write control proves the probe can still be accepted where it should be (accepted on pm_assets), so three refusals cannot mean three malformed requests.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_lxp_au_identity_after_change.mjs (gate `lxp-au-identity-after-change`) - the postgres half of this row's two-eyed instrument, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Wilfredo Malabanan while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS adversary, and this is a worker's own reading: Wilfredo Malabanan held the role worker in Baguio Textile Mills when the token was minted. MEASURED ON ai-quality.html's OWN RELATIONS: ai_cost_log (18 -> 18, and all 18 are the subject's OWN rows - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills - a person keeps their record on the way out, because a departure showing up as an ABSENCE is the opposite failure and just as bad). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. A relation this hive had no rows in is reported n/a and never counted as a pass, and the subject's membership row was captured before the first write and restored afterwards with the restoration VERIFIED by re-read. `--teeth` perturbs these expectations and the run then FAILS, so the exemptions are load-bearing rather than a green light.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_lxp_au_identity_after_change.mjs (gate `lxp-au-identity-after-change`) - the postgres half of this row's two-eyed instrument, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Wilfredo Malabanan while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS worker, and this is a worker's own reading: Wilfredo Malabanan held the role worker in Baguio Textile Mills when the token was minted. MEASURED ON ai-quality.html's OWN RELATIONS: ai_cost_log (18 -> 18, and all 18 are the subject's OWN rows - measured as Wilfredo Malabanan of Baguio Textile Mills - a person keeps their record on the way out, because a departure showing up as an ABSENCE is the opposite failure and just as bad). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. A relation this hive had no rows in is reported n/a and never counted as a pass, and the subject's membership row was captured before the first write and restored afterwards with the restoration VERIFIED by re-read. `--teeth` perturbs these expectations and the run then FAILS, so the exemptions are load-bearing rather than a green light.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. WALKED with the registered prover tools/prove_lxp_au_identity_after_change.mjs (gate `lxp-au-identity-after-change`) - the postgres half of this row's two-eyed instrument, named in live_walk_manifest's MARKERS. THE QUESTION A BROWSER CANNOT ASK: an access token is a signed bearer string with its own expiry, so revoking a membership does NOT revoke it. The only thing between a dismissed worker and their old hive is that every relation re-derives entitlement from the CURRENT membership on every read - and a browser could only reveal a failure here by holding the stale token itself. So ONE unexpired token, minted for Hector Salvador while active, was replayed across kicked and deactivated. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS oversight, and this is a supervisor's own reading: Hector Salvador held the role supervisor in Manila Electronics Assembly when the token was minted. MEASURED ON audit-log.html's OWN RELATIONS: hive_audit_log (2066 row(s) readable while the membership was active, 0 on the SAME unexpired token once it was kicked - measured as Hector Salvador of Manila Electronics Assembly). THE IDENTITY SPINE, in the same run: all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · all 4 identity relations behaved: the hive's work went to 0 on an unexpired token, and the only surviving read is the revoked member's own membership  · the same PATCH on a colleague's asset: as supervisor ACCEPTED (200) · as worker refused (200) - on one unchanged token. The row's own membership read is held to a stricter contract than silence - hive_members must keep EXACTLY the revoked person's row, so the page can say 'you were removed' and still tell that apart from an outage; returning 0 there would be a silent sign-out indistinguishable from a network failure. A relation this hive had no rows in is reported n/a and never counted as a pass, and the subject's membership row was captured before the first write and restored afterwards with the restoration VERIFIED by re-read. `--teeth` perturbs these expectations and the run then FAILS, so the exemptions are load-bearing rather than a green light.

trajectories.basis: [2026-10-28] pct -> 60. ONE token was minted for Jun Salvador while he held no seat. S1 no seat: his own hive-less rows answered 5 (the positive control) and Manila Electronics Assembly, the busiest hive, answered 0. S3 kicked: the hive went quiet (0 row(s) beyond hive_members' one row of his own) and his own rows stayed 5. S4 a global sign-out (204): the refresh grant was refused (400), so the session cannot renew, and the still-unexpired access token read 5 of his own row(s) and 0 of the hive's for the 3585s its own exp allows. S5: the granted seat was deleted and the deletion VERIFIED by re-read. THE ROW'S PERSONA IS solo-owner, AND THIS IS A SOLO OWNER'S OWN READING. MEASURED AGAINST audit-log.html's OWN RELATIONS: ai_audit_log, hive_audit_log. `--solo --teeth` demands that a seatless token read the hive, and the run then FAILS.
